pilot.who: Solaris One-One, you: a calm, dry, experienced pilot on a mask mic

wing.who: Solaris Two, the wingman: younger, quicker, laughs easily

control.who: a controller on the ground: clear, unhurried, standard phraseology

mission.who: mission control: a deep, steady veteran flight director

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Okay. Engines good, oxygen good. Solaris One-One, ready when you are.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, cleared as filed. Sky's all yours today. Have a good one.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Two's up and burning. Let's go see something nobody's seen before, huh? [chuckle]

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Rotate... gear up. [laugh] Man, I love this part.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, airborne. Climb at your discretion, contact departure. Good day.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Passing ten thousand. Smooth air. Ground's starting to look like a map.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Two's through flight level two-zero-zero. Man... it's quiet up here.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Needle's past one, we're supersonic. Somebody down there just heard a big bang. [chuckle] Sorry!

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: [laugh] Mach one! Feel that little shudder? That's the sound barrier waving goodbye.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Mach two... nose is getting warm. Everything's just sliding past underneath.

lines.speaker: mission
lines.text: Solaris, we show you hypersonic. Skin temp is climbing. Watch your heat, keep it smooth.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Mach five. Whole countries going by in minutes. This is... this is insane.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: [groan] Okay... holding it... hold it...

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: [groan] Heavy... come on... come on.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: [sigh] Okay. That one squeezed. Vision's coming back.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: You still with me, lead? [chuckle] That was a nine-G grin if I ever saw one.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: In the soup. Nothing but white. On the gauges.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Oh... popping out on top. Look at that. Whole ocean of cloud.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: And we're out! Blue sky, sun on the wings. [laugh] Never gets old.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Here comes the sun... whole horizon just turned gold. Wow.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Lead, look east. Look east. Oh, that's beautiful.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Sun's going down behind us. Everything's orange and pink... wish you could see this.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, sunset at your altitude in about two minutes. Enjoy the show.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Night side now. Cities look like spilled gold down there. And the stars... so many stars.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Dark out here. Just the glow off the instruments. Kinda peaceful, honestly.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: [gasp] Whoa, whoa. Lightning off the right side, that's close. Turning away from that cell.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, heavy weather on your route, recommend deviation. Stay safe up there.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: [fear] Ground! Ground! Pull up, pull up, come on!

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: [sigh] Oh my god. Okay. Okay... way too close. Breathe.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Lead, you okay?! I thought you were going into those rocks!

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: [laugh] You're so low I can see the treetops moving. Show-off.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Down in the weeds, hundred feet. Everything's a blur. Love it.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, wind calm, runway two-seven, cleared to land. Welcome back.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: And... we're down. Nice and soft. [sigh] What a flight.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Smooth landing, lead. I'd give it a nine. [chuckle] Maybe a nine and a half.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Passing a hundred kilometres... sky just went black. Black, in daytime. Holy...

lines.speaker: mission
lines.text: Solaris, you've crossed the Karman line. Officially, you are in space. Congratulations.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: I can see the whole curve of the Earth. That thin blue line... that's all the air there is.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Lead... it's so small. Everything we've ever known, right there under us.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Getting hot! Plasma all over the canopy. Bit of a ride here, hang on...

lines.speaker: mission
lines.text: Solaris, expect loss of signal during blackout. We'll talk to you on the other side.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Earth's getting smaller behind us. Little blue dot. Weird feeling, leaving home.

lines.speaker: mission
lines.text: Solaris, you're on your way. From here on, every word takes a little longer to reach us.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Long way still. Ever think about how quiet it is out here? Just us and the engines.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: [sigh] Coffee would be nice right about now. Long leg, this one.

lines.speaker: mission
lines.text: Solaris, all your systems look green from here. Sit back, enjoy the view.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Lead, if we meet aliens, I'm doing the talking. [chuckle] You've got a terrible radio voice.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Uh... checking fuel... we're fine. Plenty. Just enjoying the quiet.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: You know... done this a hundred times. Still gives me goosebumps.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Oh, wow... look at that.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: [gasp] You seeing this?

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Yeah... yeah. That's something else.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: I... don't even have words for that.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: [laugh] That was awesome! Again, again!

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Woo! Best job in the world, I'm telling you. [laugh]

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Mm. Nice and smooth.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, radar contact. Nice to have you with us.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Delhi Control, radar contact. Welcome to India. Himalayas off to the north.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: India! Look at all those lights... rivers like silver threads. Home, sort of.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Kathmandu Control. Over Nepal now. Eight of the ten highest mountains on Earth are right here.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Lahore Control. Over Pakistan. K2, the second highest peak in the world, is up in the north.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Dhaka Control. Over Bangladesh, the biggest river delta on the planet. All that green is the Sundarbans.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Colombo Control. Over Sri Lanka. Tea country in the hills, beaches all the way round.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Beijing Control. You are over China. The Great Wall runs for thousands of kilometres somewhere under you.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Tokyo Control. Welcome over Japan. If it's clear, Mount Fuji should be visible to the west.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Incheon Control. Over South Korea. Seoul at night is one of the brightest sights from up there.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Bangkok Control. Over Thailand. Temples, rice fields, and some very warm water down south.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Jakarta Control. Over Indonesia. Seventeen thousand islands, and more than a hundred active volcanoes.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Brisbane Centre, g'day. Welcome to Australia. Lot of red desert ahead. A lot.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Christchurch Control. Over New Zealand. Glaciers, fjords and more sheep than people.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Dubai Control. Over the Emirates. The tall one sticking up out of the city? That's the Burj Khalifa.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Jeddah Control. Over Saudi Arabia. The Empty Quarter, the largest sand sea in the world, lies to the south.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Tehran Control. Over Iran. Mountains, high desert, and cities older than most countries.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Ankara Control. Over Turkey, where Europe meets Asia. Istanbul sits right on the line.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Cairo Control. Over Egypt. Follow the green strip of the Nile, and the pyramids are just west of Cairo.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Nairobi Control. Over Kenya. The savanna below is migration country. Keep an eye out for Kilimanjaro, south.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Johannesburg Control. Over South Africa. Two oceans meet off the Cape.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Lagos Control. Over Nigeria, the most populous country in Africa. Busy skies tonight.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Casablanca Control. Over Morocco. The Atlas mountains, and beyond them, the Sahara.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Moscow Control. Over Russia. Eleven time zones wide. You could fly all day and still be here.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, London Control, good day. Over the United Kingdom. Bit of cloud, as usual.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Paris Control, bonjour. Over France. The Alps are to the east, and the Eiffel Tower is waiting in Paris.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Langen Radar. Over Germany. The Rhine valley and the Black Forest are under your left wing.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Roma Control, buongiorno. Over Italy. The boot, the Alps, and Vesuvius near Naples.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Madrid Control, hola. Over Spain. Sunshine and the Pyrenees to the north.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Zurich Control. Over Switzerland. Mountains in every direction. The Matterhorn is the pointy one.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Norway Control. Over Norway. Fjords all down the coast, and in winter, the northern lights.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Reykjavik Control. Over Iceland. Fire and ice down there. Volcanoes under glaciers.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Athinai Control. Over Greece. Thousands of islands in that blue water.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Center, radar contact. Welcome to the United States. Sky's wide open, enjoy.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Toronto Centre. Over Canada. Forests and lakes as far as you can see. Millions of lakes.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Mexico Control, buenas. Over Mexico. Volcanoes around the capital, beaches on both coasts.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Brasilia Control, bom dia. Over Brazil. The Amazon is the green that never ends.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Ezeiza Control. Over Argentina. Pampas, Andes, and down south, Patagonia.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Lima Control. Over Peru. Machu Picchu is up in those mountains, in the clouds.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Santiago Control. Over Chile. Four thousand kilometres long and barely two hundred wide.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Antarctica. Nothing but white, all the way to the horizon. Nobody calling us down here.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Feet wet over the Pacific. Biggest thing on the planet, and it's just... blue. Forever.

lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Solaris One-One, Shanwick, radar service terminated. Crossing the Atlantic. Good luck.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Over the Indian Ocean now. Nothing out here but water and a few lonely islands.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Sea ice everywhere. Cracked like a mirror. It's the top of the world, lead.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Oh... wow. Everest, right off the left wing. Whole ridge is glowing. Never getting used to this.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: There's the Eiffel Tower! [laugh] Looks like a little toy from up here.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: The pyramids... four and a half thousand years old. And we're flying past them in a jet. Unreal.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Lead... the Grand Canyon. A mile deep. Look at all those colours.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Sand dunes all the way to the horizon. The Sahara's the size of a whole continent.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: The Alps. Look at those glaciers... snow on every peak. Beautiful.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Tokyo at night... it's like a circuit board made of light. Thirty-seven million people.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Manhattan off the nose. All those towers, packed together. Hello, New York!

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Burj Khalifa, eight hundred and twenty-eight metres. And we're higher. [chuckle]

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: The Taj Mahal... white marble on the river. Built for love. Still gets me.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Mount Fuji. That perfect cone, snow on top. Just like the paintings.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: The Amazon. The river's wider than some countries. And the forest just doesn't stop.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Northern lights... green curtains moving across the sky. Oh my god. Look at them dance.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Moon, dead ahead. Grey and silent. And look... Earth rising over the rim. No borders from here.

lines.speaker: mission
lines.text: Solaris, lunar arrival. The Sea of Tranquility, where Apollo eleven landed, is on the near side. The footprints are still there.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Mars. It's really red. Rusty, dusty red. And that canyon... it would cross a whole continent back home.

lines.speaker: mission
lines.text: Solaris, Mars arrival confirmed. Olympus Mons is three times higher than Everest. Our messages are taking minutes to reach you now.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Dust storm on the horizon, lead. That thing's covering half the planet. Let's not go in there.

lines.speaker: mission
lines.text: Solaris, Venus. Surface is hot enough to melt lead and the clouds are sulphuric acid. Do not go down there.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Those clouds look like they're boiling. Yeah... I'm staying up here, thanks.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Mercury. The Sun is huge from here. Three times bigger. And the ground's all craters.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Jupiter... holy hell. Great Red Spot, dead ahead. That storm could swallow the Earth.

lines.speaker: mission
lines.text: Solaris, radiation levels are high this close to Jupiter. Keep your distance from the inner moons.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Io! There's a volcano going off right now! Look at that plume, straight up into space!

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Europa. All that ice... and an ocean underneath. If there's life out here, it might be right below us.

lines.speaker: mission
lines.text: Solaris, Ganymede. The largest moon in the solar system. Bigger than Mercury.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Callisto. Craters on top of craters. Nothing's changed here in four billion years.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Saturn. Oh... the rings. So thin, and they go on forever. Most beautiful thing I've ever seen.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Lead, those rings are ice and rock, moving fast. Careful crossing the plane. Real careful.

lines.speaker: mission
lines.text: Solaris, Titan. Thick orange haze, and lakes of liquid methane on the surface. It rains there.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Geysers! Enceladus is spraying ice right out into space. Sparkling. Wow.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Uranus. Pale blue, and tipped right over on its side. Strange, quiet planet.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Neptune. That blue... the deepest blue. Fastest winds in the solar system down there.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Pluto. There's the heart. The Sun's just a bright star from here. We're so far from home.

lines.speaker: mission
lines.text: Solaris, Ceres, in the asteroid belt. Those bright spots in the crater are salt.

lines.speaker: mission
lines.text: Solaris, you are getting very close to the Sun. Heat shields near limits. Turn away, turn away now.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: The corona... like white fire reaching out into space. Okay. That's close enough. Way close enough.

lines.speaker: mission
lines.text: Solaris, welcome home. Earth approach. It's good to hear your voice clearly again.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: There she is. Home. Blue and white and... alive. Nothing else out there looks like this.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: The black hole... light's bending all around it. I don't like this. I really don't like this.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Asteroid belt. Funny, in movies it's packed. Out here they're thousands of kilometres apart.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Look back. That speck of light? That's Earth. Everyone who ever lived... on that little dot.

lines.speaker: mission
lines.text: Solaris, your signal's taking hours to reach us now. We hear you. You're doing great out there.

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Eclipse! The Moon's sliding over the Sun... the light's going strange. Look at the corona.

lines.speaker: mission
lines.text: Solaris, solar flare in progress. Radiation spike incoming. Expect some static on this channel.

lines.speaker: wing
lines.text: Comet! Look at the tail on that thing! Millions of kilometres long!

lines.speaker: pilot
lines.text: Shooting stars... there's another one. And another. It's raining light tonight.

lines.speaker: mission
lines.text: Solaris, you are now seeing the solar system as it was, long before us. Look closely. Nothing here knows we exist yet.
